newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM to stop carrying radioactive cargo.
newsitem.headline: KLM to stop carrying radioactive cargo.

text.p: Dutch airline KLM said on Wednesday it would no longer carry radioactive materials as cargo on any passenger flights from June 27.
KLM is currently under inquiry by the Dutch transport ministry after passengers on a London-bound flight were exposed to radiation from a shipment of medical equipment last month.
"Transportation of radioactive material by air is subject to strict regulations," KLM said in a statement. "We are convinced that KLM has always conformed to these regulations."
But it said it had "a difference of interpretation" with the Dutch aviation inspectorate and was suspending shipments of such materials on passenger flights until the difference was resolved.
The case arose from a shipment of slightly radioactive medical equipment on KLM's KL129 passenger flight from Amsterdam to London on May 2.
Routine checks on arrival by British inspectors showed the shipment emitted higher levels of radiation than indicated in freight documents.
KLM is alleged to have neglected to carry out the required checks when accepting the cargo and to have failed to report the incident to Dutch civil aviation authorities.
The transport ministry said on Tuesday a closed hearing into the incident had been adjourned until July 3.
"We find it important to repeat that, in any case, for passengers on this flight of May 2 and the staff involved, there has been at most a negligible health risk," KLM said in its statement.

It said a few passengers could have received a dose of radiation of a maximum of one millisievert, compared to an average exposure of 2.1 millisieverts for a normal person from natural background radiation in a year.

KLM shares dipped slightly on the Amsterdam stock exchange on Wednesday. Dealers said the airline might be facing a claim for damages by some U.S. passengers on the affected flight. --Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 -www.racs.com
